title: First Steps in Crypto
lessons/cr-1/steps/0/body: **Cryptocurrency** is money recorded on a **blockchain**: a public ledger that no central bank controls. **Bitcoin (BTC)** is the first and biggest cryptocurrency.
lessons/cr-1/steps/1/body: Any cryptocurrency other than Bitcoin is called an **altcoin**, like **Ethereum (ETH)**. Small altcoins usually carry **far more volatility and risk**.
lessons/cr-1/steps/1/tip: The smaller a coin's market cap, the more easily its price swings up and down.
lessons/cr-1/steps/2/prompt: What do you call cryptocurrencies other than Bitcoin?
lessons/cr-1/steps/2/explanation: Altcoin means "alternative coin": any coin other than Bitcoin.
lessons/cr-1/steps/3/statement: The crypto market is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
lessons/cr-1/steps/3/explanation: Unlike forex and stocks, crypto never closes, not even on weekends.
lessons/cr-1/steps/4/explanation: A blockchain is a ledger that records every transaction, with copies held by thousands of computers.
lessons/cr-2/steps/0/body: An **exchange** is where you buy and sell crypto. While your coins sit on an exchange, **the exchange is the one really in control**.
lessons/cr-2/steps/1/body: In a **self-custody wallet**, you hold the **private key** (or seed phrase) yourself. Whoever has the private key owns the coins. **Never share your seed phrase with anyone.**
lessons/cr-2/steps/1/tip: No real support agent will ever ask for your seed phrase. Anyone who does is a scammer.
lessons/cr-2/steps/2/statement: If someone from exchange support asks for your wallet's seed phrase, you should give it to them.
lessons/cr-2/steps/2/explanation: This is one of the most common scams. With your seed phrase, anyone can take everything you own.
lessons/cr-2/steps/3/prompt: Who really owns the crypto in a wallet?
lessons/cr-2/steps/3/options/1: Whoever's name is on the wallet
lessons/cr-2/steps/3/explanation: On a blockchain, ownership means holding the private key.
lessons/cr-2/steps/4/sentence: Whoever holds the ___ has ___ of the wallet.
lessons/cr-2/steps/4/explanation: You can share your wallet address with anyone, but the private key means full control.
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/prompt: What's the safest way to store your seed phrase?
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/options/0: Write it on paper and keep it somewhere safe
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/options/1: Send it to yourself in a chat
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/options/2: Take a photo and upload it to the cloud
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/options/3: Send it to a trusted friend
lessons/cr-2/steps/5/explanation: An offline copy on paper is out of hackers' reach.
lessons/cr-3/steps/0/body: A **stablecoin** is a cryptocurrency whose price is pegged to a stable asset like the **dollar**, such as **USDT (Tether)**. In the BTC/USDT pair, you see Bitcoin's price in Tether.
lessons/cr-3/steps/1/body: Crypto prices can move **10% or more** in a single day. High volatility means more opportunity, but **much more risk**, so keep your position size smaller in crypto.
lessons/cr-3/steps/2/prompt: In the BTC/USDT pair, what is the price quoted in?
lessons/cr-3/steps/2/explanation: Just like in forex, the second currency is the unit of price: here, Tether.
lessons/cr-3/steps/3/statement: Because a stablecoin is pegged to the dollar, its price usually stays close to $1.
lessons/cr-3/steps/3/explanation: A stablecoin is built for a steady price. That's why traders park their money in it when they take profits.
lessons/cr-3/steps/4/prompt: Bitcoin fell from $60,000 to $54,000 in one day. How big was the drop in percent?
lessons/cr-3/steps/5/pairs/3/meaning: Where you buy and sell crypto
